drafts.name: Marius Arvinte

email.subject: IDEAS harness and parallel agents
email.body:
Hi Marius,

I read the IDEAS for TRACTOR post. Keeping the LLM to the translation step and making everything else deterministic, with test-suite equivalence as the yardstick, is a sensible line to draw for C to safe Rust.

Where Devin could fit is the work around that harness: it runs in its own VM, builds the project, runs the equivalence tests on each partial translation and opens a PR when a module passes. On a different language pair, Mercedes-Benz used it to cut a COBOL modernization from an estimated eight months to eight days.

Would you be up for 15 minutes comparing approaches?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: Hi Marius, I enjoyed the IDEAS for TRACTOR write-up on translating C to safe Rust. I work on coding agents for large migrations and would value comparing notes. Glad to connect.
drafts.linkedin_followup: Thanks for connecting, Marius. A question from the post that stuck with me: whether it's cheaper to translate straight to idiomatic Rust or run a refactoring pass afterwards. That second pass is the kind of bounded, test-checked work Devin handles well, since each change ships as a PR a Rust developer can review. Curious whether you've tried agents on the refactor stage yet. Happy to share what we've seen if that's useful.
